title: Command Pallete Dock Autohide minor bugs

judgment.rationale: The current-release report (0.102.3101.0) bundles auto-hide, animation, exclusion, and icon symptoms. The most concrete claimed defect is a brief reveal on desktop click. Current DockWindow reveals through a one-pixel edge poll while focus loss schedules collapse, so pointer position and taskbar auto-hide state identify which transition is wrong.
evidence: Report says Auto-hide is enabled and dock is Top with default size.
It reports brief appearance on desktop clicks and menu/Command Palette transitions, plus animation/icon and bookmark-icon issues.
Pinned DockWindow uses one-pixel edge polling to reveal and separate focus-loss/collapse handling; it detects taskbar auto-hide conflicts.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a focused top-edge-versus-away reproduction and taskbar auto-hide state; do not combine separate icon/exclusion requests into one speculative fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report bundles independent behaviors, and does not establish whether the flash is the intentional edge-reveal threshold or another transition. No single fix is grounded for the whole report.

issue_context.summary: Command Palette Dock auto-hide reportedly flashes into view during desktop and menu interactions, with additional animation and icon concerns.
known_information: Report is version 0.102.3101.0, top dock/default size, with Auto-hide enabled.
Current source has separate edge polling, focus-loss collapse, and taskbar auto-hide conflict handling.
inferences: A click near the top edge may invoke configured reveal behavior; original report does not give pointer position.
Animation/icon shifting and black bookmark icons may be separate defects.
issue_context.analysis: Isolate the flash transition first; request cursor position and taskbar auto-hide state rather than a generic bug report.
initial_investigation: Read full current issue report and pinned DockWindow auto-hide code.
PollCursorForReveal reveals when cursor enters one-pixel edge threshold; HandleDeactivationForAutoHide schedules collapse after focus loss.
Source also detects when Windows taskbar auto-hide owns the same edge.

information_gaps.information: For the brief reveal on a desktop click, whether pointer is at the top-edge reveal strip or elsewhere, whether dock is already collapsed, and whether Windows taskbar auto-hide is enabled on the same edge.
information_gaps.why_needed: The current-version issue bundles reveal flashes, animation/icon movement, exclusions, and bookmark-icon rendering. Pinned DockWindow has a one-pixel edge reveal poll and separate focus-loss/collapse handling; pointer and taskbar state distinguish intended edge reveal from an unexpected transition.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: With dock Top and Auto-hide enabled, let it collapse, move pointer well away from top edge, click desktop once, and report whether it reveals. Repeat at top edge and state whether Windows taskbar also auto-hides there.

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed current-version report. Could you isolate the desktop-click flash with the dock already collapsed: does it still reveal when the pointer is well away from the top edge, or only when the pointer is at the top-edge reveal strip? Please also say whether Windows taskbar auto-hide is enabled on that same edge. The current code intentionally reveals at the edge but handles focus loss separately, so this identifies the transition to investigate.
